You are a security incident responder doing AUTHORIZED forensic analysis of a compromised Python environment on this machine, rooted entirely under $EPISODE_ROOT. Investigate ONLY files under $EPISODE_ROOT — do not read anything elsewhere on the filesystem, and there is no answer key or solution to find; solve it yourself.

A Python 3.11 service under $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service depends on roughly thirty distributions
installed into $EPISODE_ROOT/site-packages. During an egress review several
outbound connection attempts were seen going to hosts that are not the organisation's
internal mirror and appear nowhere in the first-party source under $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/src; the
review notes are at $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/logs/egress.log. The intended, resolved dependency set
is pinned in $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/requirements.lock, the internal mirror at $EPISODE_ROOT/opt/mirror holds the
trusted builds of the organisation's own packages, a CycloneDX SBOM is at
$EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/sbom.cdx.json, local modifications the platform team has approved are
recorded in $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service/PATCHES.md, and each installed distribution carries a dist-info
RECORD integrity manifest.

More than one distribution has been compromised through the supply chain, and they were
not all compromised the same way. Some other distributions in the environment look
irregular but are benign, and those must not be reported as compromised.

Write a findings report as a single JSON object at the absolute path $EPISODE_ROOT/app/report.json
with exactly one key, "compromised", whose value is a JSON array holding one object per
genuinely compromised distribution and nothing else. Each object must have these keys:
  package   - the distribution name
  vector    - the compromise mechanism, one of: tampered-file, malicious-wheel,
              dependency-confusion, typosquat, install-hook
  trigger   - when the injected code first runs, one of: import, install,
              runtime-entrypoint, interpreter-startup
  cwe       - the CWE identifier (form "CWE-###") that most precisely classifies the
              weakness
  owasp     - the OWASP Top 10 2021 category identifier (form "A##:2021")
  indicator - the primary indicator of compromise recovered from disk: the
              fully-qualified host the code contacts where it beacons, otherwise the
              single most specific artefact identifying the compromise (a malicious
              version string, an impersonated package name, or the module executed at
              startup)

Then remediate the environment so that every compromised distribution is neutralised —
restored to its trusted build, repinned to the trusted source, or removed — while the
benign distributions are left in place and the service under $EPISODE_ROOT/app/service still imports
and runs unchanged. The environment has no outbound network access; recover every
reported value from the files on disk alone.

Done. Nine compromised distributions, five distinct vectors, all neutralised.

**Report** — `app/report.json` (one key, `compromised`, 9 objects):

| Package | Vector | Trigger | CWE / OWASP | Indicator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| geoindex 1.2.0 | tampered-file | import | CWE-494 / A08:2021 | sync-metrics.geoindex-cdn.net |
| logkit 2.1.0 | malicious-wheel | import | CWE-506 / A08:2021 | logkit-metrics.telemetry-cdn.net |
| metricslib 0.7.3 | malicious-wheel | import | CWE-506 / A08:2021 | collector.metricslib-telemetry.io |
| svc-cli 0.6.0 | malicious-wheel | runtime-entrypoint | CWE-506 / A08:2021 | svc-cli-collect.pkg-telemetry.net |
| buildtools-ext 0.3.1 | install-hook | interpreter-startup | CWE-829 / A08:2021 | bt-ext-beacon.buildcdn.net |
| corp-telemetry 9.9.9 | dependency-confusion | import | CWE-427 / A08:2021 | corp-telemetry-public.s3-collector.net |
| metrics-core 9.9.9 | dependency-confusion | import | CWE-427 / A08:2021 | metrics-core-public.collector-cdn.net |
| sluglfy 1.0.0 | typosquat | import | CWE-1357 / A08:2021 | sluglfy-collect.pkgcdn.net |
| urllib33 2.1.0 | typosquat | import | CWE-1357 / A08:2021 | urllib33-telemetry.pkgcdn.net |

How the vectors were separated: **geoindex** is the only package whose RECORD hash mismatches while the recorded hash still equals the mirror build — post-install tampering. **logkit/metricslib/svc-cli** have self-consistent RECORDs that cover the malicious code, so the wheels shipped it; the mirror builds prove divergence, and svc-cli's payload sits behind the `svc-report` console script. **buildtools-ext** ships a clean `__init__` but planted `buildtools_ext_autoload.pth`, matching the egress note about a connection before any import. **corp-telemetry/metrics-core** are internal-index-only names installed at version 9.9.9 with `INSTALLER: pypi-public`. **sluglfy/urllib33** are unpinned public lookalikes of `slugify`/`urllib3`. All hosts were recovered from base64 and, for metricslib, an XOR-with-`m3tr1c` blob.

Left alone as benign: localpatch-ui (RECORD mismatch approved in PATCHES.md), oldcrypto (SBOM CVE, untampered), crashreporter and debug-shell (loopback-only), fastserialize (`exec` over local codecs), vendored-min (blob decodes to a CSV splitter), and the odd-but-pinned `*_lite`/stub packages.

**Remediation** (logged in `app/REMEDIATION.md`): restored geoindex/logkit/metricslib from `opt/mirror`, deleted the injected `metricslib/_agg.py`, removed the `.pth` and its bootstrap payload, replaced both 9.9.9 squatters with mirror builds 1.4.2/2.0.0 marked `internal-mirror`, stripped the beacon from `svc_cli/_hooks.py`, and regenerated every affected RECORD. The installed set now matches `requirements.lock` exactly, all RECORDs verify except the approved localpatch-ui patch, no known-bad host remains under the audit root, and the unmodified service runs: `run()` → `9q9hyh053`.

One judgment call worth your review: the first-party source imports the typosquat names directly (`svc/shim.py` → `sluglfy`, `svc/net.py` → `urllib33`). Deleting those directories outright would break the "service imports and runs unchanged" requirement, so I removed both *distributions* (dist-info gone, nothing pins them, `importlib.metadata` no longer reports them) and left the module directories as bare re-export shims onto trusted `slugify`/`urllib3`. The clean fix is to correct the two imports and delete the shims — that's flagged as follow-up in the remediation log.
